text.brief: In San Francisco on April 9, 2008, the torchbearer Majora Carter pulled a small Tibetan flag from her sleeve and lost her place in the relay.
text.record: The relay reached the city weeks after the Party crushed protests in Lhasa. Officials rerouted it without notice to avoid the crowds, and the closing ceremony moved to the airport. Campus associations brought thousands of students to wave the national flag along the route, beside Tibetan and human rights protesters ([US-China Economic and Security Review Commission hearing transcript, April 30, 2009](https://www.uscc.gov/sites/default/files/transcripts/4.30.09HearingTranscript.pdf)). The flame's guards, a unit of the People's Armed Police in blue tracksuits, ran beside it in every city.
text.reading: The Party carried its security model abroad with the flame and filled the streets with flags to show a unanimity it had to organize, which is Stratagem 29. The contest over the route was a contest over who speaks for Chinese people in an American city.
text.gapText: Architecture Governance. No American authority owned the question of a foreign state's security unit working inside a city's public event.
text.fix: Set terms for any foreign security detail before a public event begins, and keep public space open to every lawful protester on equal terms.
